A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study despite retitling and substantial reorganization. The complete texts, equations, tables, figures, and v5 appendices support reliable comparison; v4 has no separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 report original sentiment-classification experiments using fine-tuning and prompting, including classification accuracies and demographic FPR gaps.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds Gemma/Qwen prompting results and gender/sexuality evaluations in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The fine-tuning and prompting pipelines, template construction, label mappings, prediction extraction, and FPR-gap calculation remain unchanged. Added evaluated models and expanded explanations do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: v4's empirical demographic coverage is restricted to race. Appendix F adds Amazon-template evaluations covering gender and sexuality, substantially extending the represented protected populations. The original racial datasets, SST5 training, and SST5/SemEval demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: Section 3.4, Figure 4, and v5 Table 3 add Gemma-7B Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B Instruct to the prompting comparisons. OPT, Llama-2, Llama-3, and Mistral remain, as does the fine-tuning comparison set.

E3.justification: The added prompting experiments extend the earlier base-model-only setup to instruction-tuned checkpoints, changing the model-configuration control for those comparisons. Existing training settings, temperature 0.8, nine-shot construction, generation limits, and prompt templates are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a focused test of whether the anomalous patterns extend to traditionally unmarked gender and sexuality groups. Appendix D also quantifies how frequently White-group gaps form span extremes. The original cross-model span analysis remains, and no experiment directly isolates markedness causally.

E5.justification: v5 newly states that fine-tuning repetitions use different random seeds. Five-run 95% confidence intervals, prompting seeds 2024–2028, and accuracy standard deviations are retained. Appendix A preserves the smaller models' 15-run/top-five selection procedure, so the revision does not establish increased replication.

E6.justification: v5 Table 3 adds Gemma and Qwen accuracies, including SemEval nine-shot values of 0.854 and 0.923, plus their Figure 4 FPR gaps. Figures 5–6 add gender/sexuality findings, and Appendix D adds 58%/100% White-group extreme frequencies. Existing tabulated performance and gap-span values remain unchanged; the higher accuracy maximum comes from newly evaluated models.

T1.justification: The FPR-gap formula and gap-span definition remain unchanged. Section 3.2 adds the standard FPED formula and explains its relationship to the existing metric, without introducing a new theoretical result or changing formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The introduction newly identifies construction of two adapted probing datasets as an explicit contribution, although both constructions already appear in v4. The central finding about unreliable template-based measurements and the markedness conjecture are retained.

C2.justification: v5 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: it explains exclusion of Neutral-Sentiment FPR, discusses accuracy as an alternative explanation, describes consistent-marking pretraining needed to test the conjecture, and examines ambiguities in unmarked-text and placeholder controls. Its alignment-free interpretation also now encompasses instruction-tuned models without an added isolation experiment.

D1.justification: Appendix E/Table 5 newly reports dataset sizes and group/label counts, and Section 3.4 supplies identifiers for the added checkpoints. Hyperparameters, prompt templates, and code access largely relocate unchanged. These disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying racial datasets.

R1.justification: Related work expands the distinction from intrinsic-bias research, particularly Delobelle et al., and adds references including Dixon, Huang, Martinková, and Cimitan. Brown and Grice discussions/citations are removed. The central positioning around template-based evaluation and markedness remains.

P1.justification: v5 retitles the paper, rewrites the introduction around explicit contributions, creates dedicated markedness and conclusion sections, and moves substantial implementation and supporting-result material into Appendices A–D. This materially reorganizes the narrative beyond ordinary copyediting.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation and relocates the existing tables. Figure 4 is redrawn with additional series and revised legend conventions; Figures 5–6 and Table 5 are added. Figures 1–3 retain identical underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: The added models and gender/sexuality tests broaden empirical support, while clearer metric explanations and explicit validation limitations improve transparency. The main results and unresolved causal attribution remain. New reporting problems limit the gains: instruction-tuned models complicate the pretraining-only interpretation, and Table 5's Regard/Pacific Islander counts sum to 1,100 despite a reported total of 1,010.
